## Overview
This piece is knitted flat, back and forth in rows. You’ll cast on 39 stitches, and the whole project—including the bind-off—is 571 rows. The gauge is 19 stitches and 38 rows per 10 cm in garter stitch, using 5 mm needles.

## Step 1: Rows 1–2
Row 1 (right side): knit all 39 stitches [k] — insert the right needle from front to back through the next stitch, wrap the yarn, and pull a loop through. The stitch count stays at 39 → 39. Row 2 (wrong side): knit all 39 stitches [k] again. The stitch count stays at 39 → 39.

## Step 2: Repeat Rows 1–2
Keep repeating Rows 1–2 until the piece measures 150 cm. That means 284 more repeats, or 568 rows (rows 3–570 of the piece). The stitch count stays at 39 → 39.

## Step 3: Finish
Bind off all 39 stitches loosely [bo] — work two stitches, lift the first over the second and off the needle, and repeat to close stitches.

## Overview
This project is knitted flat, back and forth in rows. You cast on 30 stitches, and altogether 365 rows are worked, including the bind-off. The gauge is 20 stitches and 28 rows per 10 cm in 2x2 rib, unstretched, on 4 mm needles.

## Step 1: Rows 1–2
Row 1 (right side): knit 2 [k] — insert the right needle from front to back, wrap the yarn, and pull a loop through — then work the group purl 2, knit 2 [p] seven times. Row 2 (wrong side): purl 2 [p] — with the yarn in front, insert the right needle from back to front, wrap, and pull the loop through to the back — then work the group knit 2 [k], purl 2 [p] seven times. The stitch count stays 30 → 30 on both rows.

## Step 2: Repeat Rows 1–2
Repeat Rows 1 and 2 until the piece measures 130 cm. With the gauge used, that means 181 more repeats, which is 362 rows (rows 3–364 of the piece). The stitch count stays 30 → 30.

## Step 3: Finish
Bind off all 30 stitches in pattern [bo] — work two stitches, lift the first over the second and off the needle, and repeat to close stitches.

## Overview
This piece is knitted in the round. You cast on 86 stitches and work 51 rounds in total, including the bind-off. The pattern gauge is 14 stitches and 20 rounds per 10 cm in seed stitch, on 6 mm needles.

## Step 1: Rnds 1–2
Round 1: work (k1, p1) ×43 — that means knit one [k], purl one [p], and repeat that pair of stitches 43 times around. [k] inserts the right needle front to back, wraps the yarn, and pulls a loop through; [p] is worked with the yarn in front, inserting back to front and pulling the loop through to the back. Stitches: 86 → 86.
Round 2: work (p1, k1) ×43 — purl one [p], knit one [k], repeated 43 times. Stitches: 86 → 86.

## Step 2: Repeat Rnds 1–2
Repeat Rounds 1 and 2 until the piece measures 25 cm. With the gauge used, that means 24 more repeats = 48 rounds (rounds 3–50 of the piece). Stitches: 86 → 86.

## Step 3: Finish
Bind off all 86 stitches in pattern using [bo] — work two stitches, lift the first over the second and off the needle, repeating to close stitches.

## Overview
This piece is knitted in the round. Cast on 104 stitches (size L; sizes S, M, L). In total 68 rounds are worked, including the bind-off. Pattern gauge is 21 stitches and 28 rounds per 10 cm in stockinette, on 4 mm needles.

## Step 1: Rnd 1
Rnd 1: work (k2, p2) ×26 — that means do the group of 4 stitches (knit 2 [k], purl 2 [p]) 26 times around. Knit [k] means insert the right needle from front to back through the next stitch, wrap the yarn and pull a loop through; purl [p] means with the yarn in front, insert the right needle from back to front, wrap and pull the loop through to the back. Stitches stay at 104 → 104 (no change).

## Step 2: Repeat Rnd 1
Repeat Rnd 1 until the piece measures 5 cm. With the gauge used, that means 13 more repeats = 13 rounds (rounds 2–14 of the piece). Stitches stay at 104 → 104.

## Step 3: Rnd 2
Rnd 2: work k104 — knit every stitch around. Stitches stay at 104 → 104.

## Step 4: Repeat Rnd 2
Repeat Rnd 2 until the piece measures 19 cm. With the gauge used, that means 39 more repeats = 39 rounds (rounds 16–54 of the piece). Stitches stay at 104 → 104.

## Step 5: Rnds 3–15
Rnd 3: work (k6, k2tog) ×13 — knit 6, then knit two together [k2tog] (insert the right needle knitwise into the next two stitches at once and knit them as one), repeating that group 13 times — leaving 91 stitches; Rnd 4 is a plain knit round, so it stays 91. Rnd 5: (k5, k2tog) ×13 → 78 stitches; Rnd 6: plain knit, stays 78. Rnd 7: (k4, k2tog) ×13 → 65 stitches; Rnd 8: plain knit, stays 65. Rnd 9: (k3, k2tog) ×13 → 52 stitches; Rnd 10: plain knit, stays 52; Rnd 11: (k2, k2tog) ×13 → 39 stitches; Rnd 12: plain knit, stays 39; Rnd 13: (k1, k2tog) ×13 → 26 stitches; Rnd 14: plain knit, stays 26; Rnd 15: k2tog ×13 → 13 stitches. The pattern states 91, 78, 65, 52, 39, 26, and 13 stitches respectively — all match.

## Step 6: Finish
Break the yarn and draw it through the remaining stitches.

## Overview
This project is knitted flat, back and forth in rows. You will cast on 44 stitches and work 405 rows in total, including the bind-off. The pattern gauge is 18.7 stitches and 26.6 rows per 10 cm in the eyelet pattern, blocked, on 4.5 mm needles.

## Step 1: Border row
Knit all 44 stitches [k] — insert the right needle from front to back through the next stitch, wrap the yarn and pull a loop through. Stitches 44 → 44 (no change).

## Step 2: Repeat Border row
Repeat the Border row 3 more times, which means 3 more rows (rows 2–4 of the piece). Stitches 44 → 44.

## Step 3: Rows 1–4
Row 1 (right side): knit 2, work (yarn over [yo] — wrap the yarn over the right needle once to make a new loop, leaving a small decorative hole — knit two together [k2tog] — knit the next two stitches as one — knit 3) ×8, knit 2; do that group 8 times. Stitches 44 → 44 (no change); the pattern states 44 stitches — matches.
Row 2 (wrong side): knit 2, purl 40 [p] — with the yarn in front, insert the right needle from back to front, wrap and pull the loop through — knit 2. Stitches 44 → 44.
Row 3 (right side): knit 2, work (knit 3, yarn over, slip slip knit [ssk] — slip two stitches knitwise one at a time, then knit them together through the back loops) ×8, knit 2; do that group 8 times. Stitches 44 → 44.
Row 4 (wrong side): knit 2, purl 40, knit 2. Stitches 44 → 44.

## Step 4: Repeat Rows 1–4
Repeat Rows 1–4 until the piece measures 149.9 cm, which means 98 more repeats = 392 rows (rows 9–400 of the piece). Stitches 44 → 44.

## Step 5: Final border row
Work the Final border row (right side): knit all 44 stitches. Stitches 44 → 44 (no change).

## Step 6: Repeat Final border row
Repeat the Final border row 3 more times, which means 3 more rows (rows 402–404 of the piece). Stitches 44 → 44.

## Step 7: Finish
Bind off all 44 stitches loosely [bo] — work two stitches, lift the first over the second and off the needle; repeat to close stitches.

## Overview
This pattern is knitted flat, back and forth in rows. Cast on 56 stitches and work 409 rows in total, including the bind-off. The pattern gauge is 21 stitches and 27 rows per 10 cm in feather and fan, blocked, on 5 mm needles.

## Step 1: Rows 1–4
Row 1 (right side): knit all 56 stitches [k] (insert right needle front to back, wrap, pull a loop through); stitches stay at 56. Row 2 (wrong side): purl all 56 stitches [p] (with yarn in front, insert right needle back to front, wrap, pull loop through to back); stitches stay at 56. Row 3 (right side): knit 1, then work (k2tog ×3, (yo, k1) ×6, k2tog ×3) three times, then knit 1 — that means knit two together [k2tog] (knit two stitches as one) three times, yarn over [yo] (wrap yarn over the needle to make an eyelet) and knit one six times, then knit two together three times, repeating that whole block 3 times; stitches stay at 56, and the pattern states 56 stitches — matches. Row 4 (wrong side): knit all 56 stitches [k]; stitches stay at 56.

## Step 2: Repeat Rows 1–4
Repeat Rows 1–4 until the piece measures 150 cm. With the gauge used, that means 101 more repeats = 404 rows (rows 5–408 of the piece). Stitches stay at 56.

## Step 3: Finish
Bind off all 56 stitches loosely [bo] (work two stitches, lift the first over the second and off the needle, repeat to close stitches).

## Overview
This piece is knitted flat, back and forth in rows. Cast on 24 stitches, and work 481 rows in total, including the bind-off. The gauge is 26 stitches and 34 rows per 10 cm in the cable pattern, on 4.5 mm needles.

## Step 1: Rows 1–8
Work these eight rows. On rows 1, 3, and 7, knit [k] (pull a loop through to make a stitch) 3, then repeat purl [p] (make a stitch with the yarn in front) 2, knit 6 twice, purl 2, knit 3. On row 5, knit 3, then repeat purl 2, cable 6 front [c6f] (slip 3 to a cable needle held in front, knit 3, then knit the 3 from the cable needle) twice, purl 2, knit 3. On rows 2, 4, 6, and 8, knit 3, knit 2, then repeat purl 6, knit 2 twice, knit 3. The stitch count stays at 24 throughout.

## Step 2: Repeat Rows 1–8
Repeat that same 8-row group until the piece measures 140 cm. With the gauge used, that means 59 more repeats, or 472 rows (rows 9–480). The stitch count stays at 24.

## Step 3: Finish
Bind off [bo] (work two stitches, lift the first over the second and off the needle; repeat to close stitches) all 24 stitches in pattern. This completes the 481 rows worked in total.

## Overview
This project is knitted flat, back and forth in rows. You will cast on 4 stitches and work 90 rows in total, including the bind-off. The gauge is 17 stitches and 34 rows per 10 cm in garter stitch, using 4.5 mm needles.

## Step 1: Row 1
Row 1 is worked on the right side: knit 4 stitches [k], which means inserting the right needle from front to back, wrapping the yarn, and pulling a loop through. You still have 4 stitches.

## Step 2: Inc row
The increase row is worked on the right side: knit 2 stitches, yarn over [yo], knit 2 stitches. A yarn over [yo] wraps the yarn over the needle once to make a new loop and a small decorative eyelet hole. Stitches go from 4 to 5.

## Step 3: Repeat Inc row
Repeat the increase row until there are 48 stitches. That means working the same group of stitches 43 more times, for rows 3 through 45 of the piece. Stitches go from 5 to 48.

## Step 4: Dec row
The decrease row is worked on the right side: knit 1 stitch, knit two together [k2tog], yarn over, knit two together [k2tog], knit 43 stitches. Knit two together [k2tog] means knitting two stitches as one to decrease. Stitches go from 48 to 47.

## Step 5: Repeat Dec row
Repeat the decrease row until there are 4 stitches. That means working the same group 43 more times, for rows 47 through 89 of the piece. Stitches go from 47 down to 4.

## Step 6: Finish
Bind off all 4 stitches [bo] using the standard method. Bind off [bo] means working two stitches, lifting the first over the second and off the needle, then repeating to close stitches.

## Overview
This project is knitted flat, back and forth in rows. Cast on 100 stitches (size Stroller; sizes: Stroller, Crib). You will work 177 rows in total, including the bind-off. The pattern gauge is 16 stitches and 22 rows per 10 cm in stockinette, on 5 mm needles.

## Step 1: Border row
On the right side, knit all 100 stitches [k: insert the right needle from front to back through the next stitch, wrap the yarn and pull a loop through]. The stitch count stays 100 → 100 (no change).

## Step 2: Repeat Border row
Work that same border row 9 more times, which makes 9 rows total (rows 2–10 of the piece). The stitch count stays 100 → 100.

## Step 3: Rows 1–2
Row 1 (right side): knit all 100 stitches. Stitches stay 100 → 100 (no change).
Row 2 (wrong side): knit 5, purl 90, knit 5 [p: with the yarn in front, insert the right needle from back to front through the next stitch, wrap and pull the loop through to the back]. Stitches stay 100 → 100 (no change).

## Step 4: Repeat Rows 1–2
Repeat the two-row group until the piece measures 75 cm. That means 77 more repeats, or 154 rows (rows 13–166 of the piece). Stitches stay 100 → 100.

## Step 5: Top border row
On the right side, knit all 100 stitches. Stitches stay 100 → 100 (no change).

## Step 6: Repeat Top border row
Work that top border row 9 more times, which makes 9 rows (rows 168–176 of the piece). Stitches stay 100 → 100.

## Step 7: Finish
Bind off all 100 stitches loosely [bo: work two stitches, lift the first over the second and off the needle; repeat to close stitches. In this system 'BO n' removes n stitches].
